renderings.value: Used to quote, express hearsay or define something.

The ～という grammar point is used to quote someone's words, express something you heard or read from someone else, or define and clarify the subject. It can be translated as 'called', 'that', or 'it is said'. The formation differs depending on whether it is used with a verb, い-adjective, な-adjective, or noun.
Verb-casual + という, い-Adjective + という, な-Adjective + という, Noun + という

Quotes or reports something said, or defines it (～ということ, ～というのは). Position is the difference: X + という on its own reports or defines ('they say that X'), X + という + Noun names the noun that follows it (「ハリー・ポッター」という本, 'a book called Harry Potter').
The movie has a reputation for being interesting.
In Japan, there is a tall mountain called Mount Fuji.
I heard she is doing a difficult job.
I bought a book called 'Harry Potter' at the bookstore.
Yesterday, I ate a cake that is said to be delicious.
He has a reputation for being very kind.
I want to go to a theme park called 'Disneyland' in Tokyo this summer.
